themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing you measure often shifts while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: In answer engine optimization the models call the output non-deterministic with no stable baseline, in cross-channel incrementality they say the platform reacts to the test itself, and in identity resolution and B2B buying-group signal loss they all note nobody holds the real answer key.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models again propose a single gateway or proxy with hard spend and audience caps because sends and charges cannot be undone, and the same single-exit logic shows up in downstream consent enforcement and in the shared pre-send check for journey orchestration.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people who hold the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models offer fast lanes and better prices to agents that declare themselves, on journey orchestration they point at channel owners paid on their own numbers, on the semantic context layer they call the disagreement political, and on ad supply integrity they say the market profits from unverified volume.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models say black-box platforms and already-trained models cannot show person-level proof, and in incrementality they note the platforms control both the treatment and the evidence about it.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance the models restrict writing to a library of pre-approved claims because implied meaning cannot be checked by software, and on the semantic context layer they argue a single definition of customer is the wrong target and conflicting meanings should be disclosed instead.
